text.en:
Arjun noticed that he had grown taller this year and his voice sounded different. His sister Nila said she felt moody some days.
"These are normal changes," said their teacher. "Everyone passes through adolescence."

Adolescence is the stage of life between childhood and adulthood, roughly between 10 and 19 years. Body and feelings change in this period.
Common changes include a rapid increase in height and weight, changes in the voice, growth of body hair and changes in the way we feel. These changes are controlled by chemical messengers called hormones, and they come at different ages for different people.
A balanced diet, enough sleep, exercise, cleanliness and talking to trusted adults help. Respect others and avoid harmful habits. Mood changes are normal and sharing feelings with family or teachers helps.
Adolescence is the stage between childhood and adulthood, from about ten to nineteen years.
The body grows quickly and the voice changes. Hormones control these changes.
Everyone changes at a different time. This is normal.
Eat well, sleep well, exercise, keep clean and talk to trusted adults.

problem.en: Why do some classmates grow taller earlier than others?

text.en: Hormones control the changes of adolescence.

why.en: They work at different times in each person.

text.en: So growth starts earlier for some and later for others.
There is no need to compare ourselves with others.

prompt.en: A friend feels upset about mood swings. What will you tell him?

requiredIdeas.en: Mood changes are normal in adolescence because of hormones.
Talking to a trusted adult or friend helps.

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking mood changes mean something is wrong.

points.en: Adolescence is the stage between childhood and adulthood.
Healthy habits and talking to trusted people help.
